top_cluster.headline: With under 100 days until the midterms, GOP-led mid-decade redistricting has restored the House map to a Republican tilt roughly comparable to 2018, even as Democrats and Republicans each claim distinct advantages heading into the election.
top_cluster.left_framing: No left-leaning outlet is included in this set; NPR (center-left) presents a balanced horse-race frame, citing both parties' claimed advantages without emphasizing emotion or taking a side.
top_cluster.center_framing: The Hill treats redistricting as a technical, data-driven electoral analysis, quantifying the House map's partisan lean and comparing it neutrally to 2018 without framing it as either a partisan scandal or a Republican triumph; NPR similarly frames the race as a balanced contest of competing structural and political factors.
top_cluster.right_framing: No right-leaning outlet is included in this coverage set.

blindspot_narrative: Center-left outlets are systematically avoiding the substance of the Fauci diary entry and the merits of Comey's speech defense, treating both as settled/uncontroversial rather than engaging the evidence — likely to avoid legitimizing right-wing framing. Right-leaning outlets are avoiding redistricting math that favors them (letting it pass with no coverage) while over-indexing on Democratic Party dysfunction stories (Michigan, Maine, DSA) — a pattern that suggests message discipline around 'GOP structural advantage' paired with amplification of 'Democrats in disarray.' Both sides are avoiding connecting the Comey/mail-in-voting/DNI/Iran threads into a single executive-power narrative, each preferring to cover their piece in isolation.
